newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada May housing starts rise 4.6 pct. [CORRECTED 13:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada May housing starts rise 4.6 pct. [CORRECTED 13:33 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the figure issued by the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corp, in the headline and the first paragraph to 4.6 percent from 5.0 percent.)

Canadian housing starts rose by 4.6 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 152,300 units from a revised 145,600 units (145,700 units) in April, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Monday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 149,300 units.
Actual housing starts rose to 16,435 in May from a revised 13,197 (13,207) the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said much of the increase in May housing starts could be traced to the volatile British Columbia condominium market. In British Columbia, urban starts rose more than 50 percent to 31,300 units in May, with most of the increase in multiple unit construction.
The national rise in May followed a fall of 7.8 percent in April.

"Despite these monthly fluctuations, the new housing market is still trending higher with greater demand in most provinces and low builder inventories of new and unoccupied units," said Michel Laurence, senior economist at CMHC's market analysis centre.
The provincial estimates are for centers with more than 10,000 people. The other area estimates are for centers with less than 10,000.
